comparator.sourceNotes: The Amsterdam VU-UT curriculum is represented by its 41 Amsterdam-specific positive-credit compulsory study units totaling 150 EC plus genuine generic minor 30 EC. Five compulsory 30-EC semester themes are context only and are not stacked with their children. Research Skills 5 EC precedes the BSc Assignment 12 EC under the current progression rules. University of Twente remains the awarding institution and VU the delivery partner.

core: Mathematical modelling, algorithms, signals, robotics and smart systems
Product requirements, prototyping and technological design
Material, life-cycle and resource consequences of technological systems
adjacent: Human function and neural systems for the healthcare-technology direction

selection.assessment: Two complete and substantively distinct related-fields curricula are feasible. The first combines mathematical systems, algorithms, robotics, product design, energy transition, life-cycle analysis and resource technology. The second retains the quantitative, robotic and product-design spine while replacing four energy/circular-technology courses with brain, neurobiology, perception/action and higher-function study for the explicit healthcare-technology direction. Neither is represented as Mechanical Engineering. A third structures/materials/manufacturing route cannot obtain statics, mechanics of materials, dynamics and vibrations, thermodynamics, fluid/heat transfer, metallurgy/polymers, tribology, precision engineering, manufacturing processes or the repeated mechanical build-test sequence from the workbook.

candidates.label: Computational and biological foundations for healthcare technology

alternatives.label: Smart systems, robotics & sustainable technology
alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical system models, algorithms, data methods and robotics alongside product design, life-cycle assessment, circular resource technology and renewable-energy analysis. This is a related-fields response to the smart-system and energy-transition directions, not Mechanical Engineering equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines a large quantitative/autonomous-systems spine with concrete product-design, life-cycle, resource and renewable-energy study; it does not imply mechanical formation.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, 180 EC, PPD in year one and ten advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all later mathematics, robotics and neural-network work; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes recovery, resource and renewable-system study.

alternatives.label: Computational systems, robotics & human function
alternatives.concept: Retain mathematical systems, algorithms, visual data, robotics and product design while studying brain organisation, neurobiology, sensory-motor processing and higher cognitive function as foundations for the evidenced healthcare-technology direction. Medical-device design and mechanical construction remain explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: Four neuroscience/human-function courses replace the energy, life-cycle and recovery application strand, yielding a genuine computational-biological direction without claiming medical-device engineering.

progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, 180 EC, PPD in year one and ten advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all later mathematics, robotics and neural-network work; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and Earth’s Resources. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Perception & Action and Higher Order Functions; Neurobiology is placed before the later sensory-motor course.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction: climate and renewable-energy study, life-cycle analysis and recycling/recovery technology are replaced by brain/behaviour foundations, neurobiology, perception/action and higher cognitive functions. These changes implement the explicit healthcare-technology choice.

blocks: Both establish calculus and linear-algebra foundations for quantitative system models; the external course is embedded in mechanical engineering.
UCR directly develops matrix, vector-space and linear-transformation methods; the external component combines these with further calculus.
UCR provides numerical equation and differential-equation methods relevant to finite-element computation, but not elasticity theory or finite-element mechanics.
Both develop differential-equation methods; UCR also covers multivariable and complex analysis without a mechanics application sequence.
Both analyse systems through mathematical models; UCR directly covers transfer functions, state-space and signal flow.
Both provide probability and statistics for quantitative modelling and research.
UCR studies robot kinematics, planning and manipulation, with partial control-system relevance; it does not reproduce control engineering or mechatronic hardware.
Both use a team design-and-development process involving requirements, modelling and prototyping; UCR does not reproduce structural/mechanical design or manufacturing.
Energy, life cycles, materials and resources
Both directly evaluate environmental impacts across product or process life cycles.
Both address renewable-energy technologies; UCR emphasises technical/economic system assessment rather than mechanical energy conversion.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives provide substantial mathematical, computational, robotic, product-design and application study. They do not supply the target’s mechanics, thermodynamics, materials/manufacturing, thermal-fluid, precision-design, laboratory and repeated build-test formation; neither is a Mechanical Engineering qualification.
